A team of synthetic biologists at BNext Bio reported that an experiment aimed at creating a minimal cell unexpectedly yielded a fully functional “cell factory.”  In a post on the company’s blog, the researchers described how a modular genetic circuit, designed to simplify the genome, inadvertently activated a metabolic pathway that produced high levels of a target compound—an engineered biofuel precursor.  The discovery emerged during routine testing of the chassis’ viability, when the team observed an unanticipated, robust output of the desired product.

The synthetic cell was constructed from a stripped‑down genome and a set of engineered regulatory elements.  A miswired promoter, originally intended to keep the pathway dormant, instead drove constitutive expression of the enzymes needed for the biosynthetic route.  The result was a self‑sustaining production system that could convert simple sugars into the biofuel precursor at yields comparable to, or exceeding, those of conventional microbial factories.  The team plans to refine the genetic architecture, assess scalability, and evaluate safety protocols before moving toward industrial trials.

This accidental breakthrough underscores both the potential and the unpredictability of synthetic biology.  By turning a minimal cell into an efficient production platform, the researchers have opened a new route for sustainable chemical manufacturing.  The findings, which have attracted attention on platforms such as Hacker News, may prompt further investment in minimal‑cell technologies and accelerate the development of next‑generation bioproduction systems.
author: Hacker News

title: Rails 8: Features, Requirements and Upgrade Path
content:
Ruby on Rails 8 was unveiled by the Rails core team in a recent AppSignal blog post, marking the next major milestone for the popular web‑framework. The release introduces a suite of performance‑enhancing changes, including a new default for the Active Record query cache and a streamlined query planner that reduces database round‑trips for common patterns. Rails 8 also drops the legacy Ruby 2.6 support, tightening the Ruby version requirements to 3.1 and above, which allows the framework to leverage newer language features such as pattern matching and refined keyword argument handling.

Key functional upgrades focus on developer ergonomics and modern web standards. Hotwire integration has been deepened, with built‑in support for Turbo Streams in the scaffold generator and a new “Turbo‑Friendly” form builder that automatically emits stream updates. The console has been revamped with a faster startup time and built‑in support for the new “rails console --sandbox” mode, enabling developers to experiment without persisting changes. Additionally, Rails 8 introduces a new default for Action Mailer, switching to a more secure SMTP configuration and adding built‑in support for HTML‑only emails.

The community has responded positively, with early adopters noting a measurable drop in page load times and a smoother upgrade path from Rails 7. The release is slated for full support in the next quarterly cycle, with the Rails 8 beta already available for testing. Developers are encouraged to review the migration guide on the Rails website to address deprecations and take advantage of the new features as they transition to the latest stable version.
author: Hacker News

title: Better AI code comment detector
content:
A new AI‑based comment classifier has attracted attention on the technology forum Hacker News, where a post titled “Better AI Comment Classifier” received 11 up‑votes and 5 comments. The article describes a system that uses advanced natural‑language processing techniques to automatically categorize user comments, aiming to improve moderation workflows and reduce the need for manual review. The authors highlight that the classifier can distinguish between constructive discussion, spam, and potentially harmful content with higher precision than existing models.

The discussion on Hacker News notes that the classifier was trained on a diverse dataset of millions of comments from multiple platforms, and that its performance was benchmarked against several baseline algorithms. Reviewers on the thread point out the model’s ability to handle nuanced language and its potential for integration into real‑time moderation tools. Some commenters also raise questions about the ethical implications of automated content filtering and the need for transparency in the training data.

Overall, the post and its subsequent comments suggest that the new AI comment classifier is generating interest among developers and researchers who are looking for more reliable automated moderation solutions. The conversation underscores the ongoing push toward smarter, data‑driven tools that can help online communities manage user-generated content more efficiently.
author: Hacker News

title: GNU Radio in the Browser
content:
GNU Radio World, the community‑driven hub for software‑defined radio developers, has announced the release of its latest version of the GNU Radio toolkit. The update, detailed on the site’s main page (https://gnuradioworld.com/), brings a host of new features and performance improvements, including enhanced signal‑processing blocks, expanded hardware support, and a streamlined build system that simplifies deployment on modern Linux distributions. The release notes highlight a focus on stability and backward compatibility, ensuring that existing projects can upgrade without extensive refactoring.

The announcement quickly attracted attention from the broader open‑source community, with the post appearing on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49628576). The discussion received 17 points and four comments, reflecting a modest but engaged response. Contributors praised the expanded documentation and the inclusion of a new Python API wrapper, while a few users requested additional tutorials for the new hardware drivers. Overall, the update is seen as a solid step forward for the GNU Radio ecosystem, reinforcing its position as a leading platform for rapid prototyping of radio systems.

Looking ahead, the developers plan to continue refining the toolkit in the coming months, with a roadmap that includes support for emerging SDR hardware and deeper integration with machine‑learning frameworks. By maintaining an open‑source development model and fostering community input, GNU Radio World aims to keep the toolkit at the forefront of research and commercial applications in wireless communications.
author: Hacker News

title: Anthropic Developing Predictive Surveillance System for Activists
content:
On September 9, 2026, Prospect.org published an article detailing a new artificial‑intelligence system developed by Anthropic that is designed to monitor activist activity. The system employs advanced natural‑language‑processing models to scan public social‑media posts, messaging apps, and other digital communications for keywords, sentiment patterns, and network connections that could indicate coordinated political or social‑justice campaigns. According to the report, Anthropic’s technology can aggregate data from multiple platforms, flag potential “organizing” content, and provide real‑time alerts to users who have subscribed to the service.

The article notes that while Anthropic frames the tool as a means to help law‑enforcement agencies and corporate security teams identify threats, the same capabilities can be used to surveil dissenting voices. Activist groups and privacy advocates have expressed concern that the system could be deployed without adequate oversight, potentially violating civil‑liberties and data‑protection laws. The piece also highlights that the discussion has already begun on the Hacker News community, where the story has accumulated 62 points and 19 comments, reflecting a mix of technical curiosity and apprehension about the broader implications of AI‑driven surveillance.

In summary, Anthropic’s new AI monitoring platform represents a significant development in digital surveillance technology, raising questions about the balance between security interests and individual privacy rights. The article’s coverage and the ensuing online debate underscore the growing scrutiny of AI applications that can track and analyze activist networks, and the need for clear regulatory frameworks to govern their use.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI Claims Agents Solved Major Math Problem Amid Controversy
content:
OpenAI announced that its new AI agents have reportedly solved one of the most significant unsolved problems in mathematics, sparking a swift debate across the research community. The company released a brief statement outlining the algorithmic approach and presenting preliminary results that, according to OpenAI, confirm a long‑standing conjecture. The claim was accompanied by a demonstration of the agents’ reasoning steps, which the firm says were fully traceable and reproducible.

Mathematicians and AI experts responded with caution. Several leading researchers highlighted that the proof, while intriguing, lacks the rigorous peer‑review and formal verification required for acceptance in the field. Critics pointed out that the agents’ internal logic, though documented, may still contain subtle gaps that only a human‑led scrutiny could uncover. OpenAI has invited independent reviewers to examine the evidence and has pledged to release the full dataset and code under an open‑source license to facilitate external validation.

The controversy underscores the growing tension between rapid AI progress and the traditional standards of mathematical proof. If verified, the agents’ success could herald a new era where machine‑generated proofs become a routine tool for tackling deep theoretical questions. Until the claim is independently confirmed, however, the mathematical community remains skeptical, emphasizing the need for transparent, collaborative verification before such breakthroughs can reshape the discipline.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Kepler Computing Announces New Chip Design to Alleviate Memory Supply Shortage
content:
Kepler Computing announced that its new chip‑design methodology, coupled with a proprietary material it has developed, could alleviate the supply bottlenecks that have driven memory prices to record highs. The company said the approach allows for more efficient use of raw silicon and reduces the number of process steps needed to fabricate high‑density memory cells, potentially shortening lead times for both DRAM and NAND flash production.

According to Kepler’s spokesperson, the proprietary material—an advanced high‑k dielectric—provides superior charge retention and lower leakage than conventional substrates, enabling tighter packing of memory cells without compromising performance. The firm claims that early prototypes demonstrate a 15‑percent increase in storage density and a 10‑percent reduction in manufacturing cost compared to current industry standards. Industry analysts note that if the technology can be scaled, it could help meet the surging demand for data center memory and consumer storage amid ongoing supply chain disruptions.

Kepler is currently partnering with several semiconductor manufacturers to integrate the new material into pilot production lines. While the company has not yet released commercial products, it expects that widespread adoption of its design framework could stabilize memory pricing over the next 12 to 18 months, easing pressure on both producers and consumers in the rapidly expanding digital economy.
author: Wired

title: Asus Cetra Open Earbuds Now $206.99 After $22 Discount
content:
Asus has released the Cetra Open wireless earbuds, a budget‑friendly option that blends gaming and everyday audio use. Priced at $206.99 on Amazon and Best Buy after a $22 discount, the earbuds feature an open‑style design that lets ambient sound mix with in‑game audio, a feature appreciated by users who prefer situational awareness while playing or listening to podcasts. The earbuds are compatible with a wide range of devices, including the Steam Deck, PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and smartphones, and connect effortlessly via Bluetooth.

Key technical highlights include a USB‑C 2.4 GHz transmitter that doubles as a 60‑W passthrough charger, allowing users to charge their devices while maintaining audio connectivity. The earbuds also offer respectable battery life and extensive customization options through a mobile or browser‑based app. A reflective band is included to link the earbuds together behind the neck, enhancing visibility and stability during movement.

Overall, the Cetra Open delivers solid audio performance, flexible connectivity, and practical features for both gamers and casual listeners, positioning it as a competitive choice in the mid‑range wireless earbud market.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla Cybercab Blocks Narrow Road Near Austin Swimming Hole
content:
A Tesla Cybercab has become the focus of a traffic snarl outside a popular swimming hole in Austin, Texas, after the electric vehicle partially blocked a narrow road that is heavily used by visitors. The gold‑painted two‑seater, which is part of Tesla’s long‑anticipated Cybertruck‑derived lineup, was seen idling with its lights flashing while a line of sweaty, frustrated park‑seekers gathered around it. The vehicle’s presence disrupted the flow of traffic and drew the attention of nearby pool‑goers who were trying to enjoy a brief respite from the heat.

The incident highlights the growing challenges of integrating new, large electric vehicles into existing urban infrastructure. Tesla’s Cybercab, designed for short‑range urban use, is reportedly larger than many conventional cars, and its size has raised concerns among city planners and local residents. While the company has touted the vehicle’s advanced technology and compact footprint, the blockage at the swimming hole underscores the need for clearer guidelines on parking and road use for such unconventional vehicles.

City officials have not yet issued a statement regarding the incident, but the event has sparked discussion among Austin residents about the impact of emerging automotive technologies on public spaces. As Tesla continues to roll out its new models, the company and local authorities may need to collaborate on solutions that balance innovation with the practical realities of shared roadways.
author: The Verge

title: Nintendo Announces Metroid Ravenous for Switch 2
content:
Nintendo announced a new 2‑D Metroid title for the Switch 2, titled **Metroid Ravenous**, which will launch on **January 28, 2027**. The game builds on the mechanics of *Metroid Dread* while adding fully rendered 3‑D environments and a more cinematic presentation. Players will again control Samus Aran, who can roll into Morph Ball form, parry enemies, and now appears to absorb energy from foes to sustain herself, a feature highlighted in Nintendo’s marketing copy with the tagline “eat or be eaten.”

Key gameplay elements include a roster of new adversaries ranging from gigantic creatures to a squad of futuristic, caped fighters. The title promises intense action sequences and a variety of enemy types that challenge the player’s reflexes and strategy. The blend of 2‑D gameplay with 3‑D visuals aims to deliver a fresh take on the series while maintaining the core exploration and combat style that fans expect.

With its release set for early 2027, *Metroid Ravenous* positions itself as a major addition to the Metroid franchise, offering both familiar mechanics and new features that could broaden the series’ appeal on the upcoming Switch 2 platform.
author: The Verge

title: Framework Lowers RAM Prices for Laptop 13 Pro
content:
Framework has announced a temporary reduction in the price of RAM for its Laptop 13 Pro, a move aimed at easing the impact of the ongoing semiconductor shortage. Following a July price hike for the laptop’s memory, the company secured a limited supply of Micron 32‑GB and 64‑GB LPCAMM2 memory modules at a lower cost. The manufacturer said it will pass those savings on to customers, lowering the cost of the memory for both units already shipped and a subset of pending pre‑orders.

The price cut applies only to the specific memory configurations that Framework has secured, and the new rates remain above the original launch price of the Laptop 13 Pro. The company emphasized its commitment to keeping its devices accessible in a challenging supply‑chain environment, noting that the reduction is a “rare, positive update” amid the broader component shortage. The announcement was reported by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Google adds live NFL game feed to mobile search
content:
Google has unveiled a new Live Game Feed for the National Football League, launching as the regular season kicks off tonight. The feature, visible on mobile devices as a red “Live” icon, delivers real‑time recaps of the ongoing game, play‑by‑play commentary, social media highlights, video clips, and AI‑powered insights that analyze key moments. Users can also view a carousel of scores for other games currently in progress, making it easier to keep track of multiple matchups simultaneously.

In addition to NFL coverage, the update now supports college football games and will roll out support for additional languages later in the month. Google has enhanced the statistics display, showing player leaders in categories such as passing touchdowns and rushing yards, and refining the way performance data is presented. The new feed is available immediately in English on mobile platforms, with further language options expected soon.

With these additions, Google aims to provide fans with a comprehensive, on‑the‑go view of football action, combining traditional play‑by‑play updates with modern AI analysis and a streamlined interface for quick score checks across multiple games.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Unveils iPhone 18 and Foldable Design at CEO John Ternus' Keynote
content:
Apple is set to host its first iPhone keynote under newly appointed CEO John Ternus, who previously served as Apple’s vice‑president of hardware engineering at WWDC 2019. The event is widely regarded as a potential turning point for the company, with analysts noting that it could usher in a new era of design and technology.

Rumors point to a foldable iPhone as the headline announcement, accompanied by updates to iOS, new Apple Watch models, and refreshed AirPods. Ternus has described the launch as “a huge launch… That’s going to be phenomenal,” hinting at a bold product strategy that may also include unconventional elements not seen in past Apple events. The photo accompanying the announcement, taken by Brittany Hosea‑Small and released via AFP/Getty Images, shows Ternus in a former Apple role, underscoring the continuity and change within the company’s leadership.

The keynote will be closely watched by investors, industry analysts, and consumers alike, as Apple seeks to redefine its flagship product line and set the stage for future innovations in the smartphone and wearables markets.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Announces iPhone 18 Lineup and First Foldable at September 9 Event
content:
Apple will stage its “Surprise and Shine” launch on September 9 at 1 p.m. ET (10 a.m. PT), where it is expected to unveil the first iPhone 18 models, including Apple’s inaugural foldable device, the rumored “iPhone Duo.” The event will also mark the first public appearance of John Ternus as Apple’s CEO, following his succession of Tim Cook on September 1. Ternus, who had led Apple’s hardware engineering, highlighted the upcoming hardware lineup in his first staff memo as chief executive.

In addition to the new iPhones, the September 9 gathering may feature updates to the Apple Watch, AirPods, and possibly an Apple TV refresh or new smart‑home hardware. The announcement of a foldable iPhone is widely seen as a pivotal moment for Apple, signaling a new era of product innovation under Ternus’s leadership. Industry analysts and consumers alike will be watching closely to gauge how the new CEO’s vision translates into tangible releases.

The event is poised to set the tone for Apple’s next chapter, with the company’s first major product reveal under Ternus’s stewardship. Updates and live coverage will be available through Apple’s official channels and independent tech outlets, providing real‑time insight into the company’s forthcoming offerings.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox Reintroduces Classic Boot Animations in New Insider Test
content:
Microsoft has begun testing a suite of new features on its Xbox consoles with the Insiders program. The updates let testers customize the console’s boot animation, choosing from the original Xbox One screen, the Xbox One X startup, the original Xbox Series X/S animation, or the new “We Are Xbox” sequence. The company also added more personalization options for user badges, a refreshed local search function, and clearer voice‑chat audio.

In addition to visual tweaks, the test build improves Remote Play performance and introduces the ability to download cloud games while they are being streamed. These enhancements aim to streamline the gaming experience on the console, providing smoother transitions between local and cloud gameplay and better audio clarity for multiplayer sessions.

The rollout is limited to the Insiders program and does not include boot screens from the original Xbox or Xbox 360, which are restricted to Xbox One and later models. Users who opt into the program will be able to experiment with these new features and provide feedback to Microsoft before a broader release.
author: The Verge

title: NOAA Prioritizes Commercial Fishing Over Conservation
content:
Critics have voiced concerns that the newly announced agenda may erode established science‑based regulations and diminish existing marine protection measures. The opposition, which includes environmental advocacy groups and several scientific organizations, argues that the proposed changes could undermine the evidence‑driven framework that currently guides policy decisions affecting ocean health and biodiversity.

Stakeholders warn that weakening these safeguards could expose marine ecosystems to heightened risks from overfishing, habitat degradation, and pollution, potentially reversing recent gains in conservation. The debate over the agenda highlights a broader tension between policy objectives and the need to preserve scientifically validated environmental standards, with officials indicating that the proposals are intended to streamline regulatory processes while opponents call for a more cautious approach.
author: Ars Technica

title: Bipartisan Lawmakers Urge Ban on Hack-for-Hire Firms
content:
Three Indian companies have been charged with employing hackers to acquire confidential data that could be used to influence the outcomes of ongoing litigation. According to court filings, the firms allegedly directed cyber‑attacks against competitors and regulatory bodies, extracting sensitive documents and communications that were then leveraged as evidence or leverage in legal disputes. The accusations were first reported by a national investigative agency, which cited forensic analysis of server logs and intercepted communications as evidence of the illicit activity.

The case underscores a growing concern over cyber‑exploitation in commercial litigation. Analysts note that the use of stolen information to sway court decisions undermines the integrity of the legal process and may expose the companies to civil liability, criminal prosecution, and regulatory sanctions. While the companies have denied any wrongdoing, the investigation is ongoing, and the court has imposed temporary restrictions on their access to certain data repositories pending a full hearing.

If the allegations are proven, the firms could face substantial fines, mandatory compliance overhauls, and potential criminal charges against senior executives. The case highlights the need for stricter cybersecurity protocols in the corporate sector and may prompt regulators to tighten oversight of data handling practices in litigation contexts.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Spend per Employee Falls at Major Firms in August
content:
Hyperscalers that have invested heavily in generative AI are finding that the economics of adoption are not matching their expectations.  Token‑pricing models, once a major cost driver for large‑language‑model usage, have fallen sharply as newer, more efficient architectures are released.  This, coupled with the availability of cheaper, specialized models, has reduced the overall spend required to run AI workloads.  As a result, many enterprises are deploying generative AI at a slower pace and at a lower per‑employee cost than the hyperscalers projected when they launched their initial cloud‑based AI platforms.

The shift is evident in the way companies are budgeting for AI.  Instead of allocating large, upfront capital for high‑volume token consumption, firms are now opting for a mix of on‑premise inference engines and cost‑effective, fine‑tuned models that deliver comparable performance at a fraction of the price.  This trend has also led to a more measured rollout of AI tools across the workforce, with pilot programs and targeted use cases taking precedence over blanket, organization‑wide deployments.  The result is a more conservative spend trajectory, with many companies reporting a 30‑40 % reduction in AI operating expenses compared to the first year of adoption.

While the reduced cost of AI services is a win for businesses, it also signals a recalibration of the hyperscalers’ growth strategy.  The companies now face the challenge of sustaining revenue streams from AI services that are becoming increasingly affordable and competitive.  To keep pace, they are expanding their focus to include higher‑value, enterprise‑specific solutions and deeper integration services, aiming to capture the premium segment of the market that still demands advanced, customized AI capabilities.
author: TechCrunch

title: Uber Invests $10M in Carrum at $168M Valuation
content:
Carrum Mobility, a leading Indian fleet operator, now manages roughly 5,100 vehicles across the country, making it Uber’s largest partner for the premium Uber Black service. The partnership, which has expanded over the past year, allows Uber to offer high‑end rides with a larger, more reliable supply of vehicles in key urban markets.

The fleet partnership underscores Uber’s strategy to strengthen its premium offerings in India, where demand for upscale transportation has grown steadily. Carrum’s extensive network of vehicles—ranging from luxury sedans to premium SUVs—provides the company with the capacity to meet surge periods and maintain the high‑quality standards expected by Uber Black customers.

By aligning with Carrum Mobility, Uber can enhance service availability and reliability for its premium segment while supporting Carrum’s growth as a major player in India’s ride‑hailing ecosystem. The collaboration is expected to benefit both companies as they continue to expand their presence in the country’s competitive mobility market.
author: TechCrunch

title: Shipt Adds AI Shopping Assistant to Delivery Service
content:
Shipt has announced a new feature that lets shoppers use the platform’s AI assistant to build customized grocery carts for specific occasions. According to the company, users can simply request a “tailgate cart for 25 people with brunch items” or a “cart for easy school lunches and after‑school snacks,” and the assistant will automatically populate the cart with appropriate products and quantities.

The assistant pulls from Shipt’s extensive inventory and can suggest items that fit the requested theme, such as pre‑made sandwiches, beverage options, and snack packs for the tailgate, or protein‑rich foods and healthy snacks for school lunches. Shipt says the feature streamlines the shopping experience, reducing the time shoppers spend manually adding items and ensuring they have everything needed for their event.

By leveraging AI to anticipate shoppers’ needs, Shipt aims to make grocery ordering more efficient and personalized. The company plans to expand the assistant’s capabilities to cover additional event types and dietary preferences in the coming months.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns Over AI Extinction Fears
content:
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from the company in early September, citing growing concerns about the existential risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. Coxon, who had worked on safety and alignment projects at Anthropic for several years, said that the pace at which the organization and the broader industry were developing increasingly powerful models outstripped the available safety protocols and oversight mechanisms.

In a statement released by the company, Coxon urged the AI community to adopt “pacing agreements” that would coordinate the release schedules of new technologies across laboratories. He argued that such agreements could help prevent a race to the bottom in safety standards and provide a framework for shared risk assessment. The call follows a series of high‑profile warnings from AI researchers and ethicists about the potential for rapid, uncontrolled deployment of systems that could surpass human control.

The resignation has prompted discussions within the AI safety community about formalizing collaborative safety frameworks. While Anthropic has not yet announced a replacement for Coxon, it has pledged to review its internal safety protocols and to engage with other research institutions on the proposed pacing agreements. The move underscores the increasing pressure on AI developers to balance innovation with robust risk mitigation.
author: TechCrunch

title: InDrive Expands Beyond Ride-Hailing with Successful Ad Platform
content:
InDrive’s newly launched advertising platform, which went live in July 2025, has quickly become a significant revenue stream for the ride‑hailing company. Within its first year, the service has delivered more than 2 billion ad impressions to users across the network, underscoring the scale of its reach.

The platform has also attracted a robust advertiser base, with over 2,000 paying clients reporting each month. These advertisers range from local businesses to national brands, all leveraging InDrive’s in‑app placement to target commuters in real time. The rapid uptake suggests that the company’s data‑driven ad solutions are resonating with marketers looking for high‑frequency, location‑based exposure.

The growth in both impressions and advertiser participation signals a promising expansion of InDrive’s monetization strategy beyond its core transportation services. As the company continues to refine its targeting capabilities, it is poised to deepen its foothold in the mobile advertising market while providing drivers and passengers with a more integrated in‑ride experience.
author: TechCrunch

title: Instinct AI Adds Email Capability for Users
content:
Instinct has unveiled a new email feature that empowers its AI agent to create and manage email accounts, contact businesses, and handle support requests on behalf of users. The update expands the platform’s automation capabilities, allowing the agent to perform routine communications tasks that previously required manual input.

The feature enables the AI to set up new email addresses, draft and send messages to vendors or service providers, and respond to incoming support tickets. Users can delegate routine outreach and follow‑up activities, while the agent logs interactions and tracks responses within Instinct’s dashboard. The system also includes safeguards to ensure compliance with privacy regulations and to maintain user control over sensitive information.

With this addition, Instinct aims to streamline workflow for professionals who rely on frequent email communication. By delegating account creation and support handling to the AI, the platform promises to reduce administrative overhead and accelerate response times for its users.
author: TechCrunch

title: Experts warn AI could pose existential risk within a decade
content:
Industry insiders have issued a series of urgent warnings in the past 48 hours, calling for stronger regulatory measures on artificial superintelligence (ASI). Prominent technologists and AI researchers on both sides of the Atlantic have suggested that the potential dangers of ASI could surpass those of nuclear weapons, citing scenarios ranging from a “Chernobyl‑sized catastrophe” to a more extreme projection that there may be a greater than 10 % chance of AI causing human extinction within the next decade. The alerts have been amplified by recent media coverage that frames the technology, still widely perceived as an advanced search engine, as a possible existential threat.

The statements have intensified calls for immediate policy action, with experts urging governments and international bodies to develop comprehensive oversight frameworks, safety standards, and risk‑assessment protocols for advanced AI systems. While the precise probability of the worst‑case outcomes remains debated, the consensus among the warning voices is that the rapid pace of AI development outstrips current safeguards, creating a window of vulnerability that could lead to irreversible harm. Policymakers are now faced with balancing innovation incentives against the need for stringent controls to mitigate the highlighted risks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: White House removes Tetris-style “Build The Wall” game over copyright concerns
content:
The Tetris Company issued a statement on Monday emphasizing its strict stance on copyright infringement after reports surfaced that a newly released mobile title featured gameplay mechanics and visual elements closely resembling the classic puzzle game. In the statement, the company clarified that it had no involvement in the development, distribution, or promotion of the disputed app and reiterated that any unauthorized use of its intellectual property would be addressed through appropriate legal channels.

Legal experts note that the company’s response aligns with its history of actively protecting the Tetris brand, which is protected by multiple patents and trademarks worldwide. The Tetris Company’s declaration serves as a warning to developers who may incorporate recognizable aspects of the game without permission, underscoring the firm’s commitment to enforce its rights and maintain the integrity of the Tetris franchise.
author: BBC Technology

title: China reaffirms One-China principle amid UN resolution dispute
content:
Beijing reiterated its commitment to the One‑China principle after a renewed diplomatic dispute over the interpretation of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758, the 1971 resolution that affirmed the People’s Republic of China as the sole lawful representative of China at the United Nations. The Chinese foreign ministry issued the statement in response to recent calls by several member states and non‑governmental organizations to allow the island of Taiwan, officially the Republic of China, to participate in UN activities under a separate designation.

The Chinese government warned that any attempt to reinterpret the resolution or to grant Taiwan independent representation would contravene the One‑China principle and undermine the legal framework established by the UN in 1971. Beijing’s reaffirmation comes as the United Nations prepares for upcoming sessions where the status of Taiwan’s participation is expected to be raised, signaling that the issue will remain a point of contention in multilateral forums.
author: Euronews

title: Attacks on education rise globally, hindering children's learning
content:
Worldwide attacks on education have risen sharply, with schools and other learning facilities increasingly targeted in conflict zones. Reports from international monitoring bodies indicate that thousands of institutions have been damaged or destroyed over the past year, disrupting the education of millions of children and exacerbating existing inequalities in access to learning.

Dr. Maleiha Malik of the Education Above All Foundation acknowledged that while it remains feasible to keep children engaged in learning through alternative and remote methods, the physical and psychological damage inflicted by conflict is not easily remedied. She emphasized the need for coordinated reconstruction efforts and sustained investment in safe learning environments to restore the long‑term educational prospects of affected communities.
author: Euronews

title: Call My Agent film spinoff features George Clooney and Eva Longoria
content:
Film critic Manon Kerjean of FRANCE 24 has outlined her selections among the French entries competing at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, while also surveying recent releases in French cinema. Her commentary highlights a range of narratives, from the festival‑bound titles to new domestic offerings, underscoring the breadth of contemporary French filmmaking.

Kerjean draws attention to “15/18,” a drama set within a psychiatric unit that confronts mental‑health issues, and “A Woman’s Life,” which features César‑winner Léa Drucker as a woman whose meticulously ordered existence is disrupted by an unexpected stranger. She also previews Arthur Hariri’s “The Unknown,” a speculative piece in which two strangers awaken in each other’s bodies, and offers her perspective on the highly anticipated “Call My Agent,” a continuation that resumes five years after the conclusion of the popular Netflix series. Kerjean’s selections provide a snapshot of the thematic diversity and creative vigor shaping French cinema this season.
author: France 24

title: France's National Rally dismisses policeman after racist, homophobic remarks captured on bodycam
content:
France’s far‑right National Rally (RN) expelled a police officer from its ranks on Wednesday after body‑camera footage surfaced showing him uttering racist, homophobic and sexist slurs. The video, which quickly spread on social media, prompted the party’s leadership to terminate the member’s affiliation, citing a zero‑tolerance policy for conduct that contradicts the RN’s public commitment to law and order.

The incident arrives as the RN seeks to shed the extremist reputation of its National Front origins ahead of the 2027 presidential election, a process already under scrutiny from opponents and civil‑rights groups. Party officials emphasized that the expelled officer acted independently and reiterated their ongoing effort to present a mainstream, respectable platform, while analysts note that the controversy could revive questions about the depth of the RN’s ideological transformation and its impact on voter perception.
author: France 24

title: 38 skeletons found in pre-Incan Peruvian tomb
content:
Archaeologists working in the northern highlands of Peru have uncovered a near‑intact pre‑Incan tomb that contained the remains of 38 individuals together with a collection of gold and copper artifacts. The burial site, located in a region historically linked to the Chimu culture, was discovered during a systematic survey of the area and is being examined by a team from the National University of San Marcos in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture.

Analysis of the skeletal material indicates that the tomb housed an elite member of the Chimu civilization, which thrived between 900 and 1470 AD, alongside other individuals who likely served as attendants or laborers. The presence of high‑status metal objects suggests complex funerary practices and a hierarchical society, offering new insight into the social organization and material wealth of the Chimu before the rise of the Inca Empire. Researchers plan further excavation and laboratory testing to better understand the tomb’s chronology and the broader cultural context of the find.
author: France 24

title: New York releases documents showing city withheld air toxicity information after 9/11
content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Tuesday that the municipal government will release tens of thousands of documents indicating that city officials did not fully disclose their knowledge of airborne toxic hazards following the September 11, 2001 attacks. The disclosure, scheduled ahead of the 25th anniversary of the attacks that claimed 2,977 lives, is intended to provide greater transparency about the environmental conditions at Ground Zero and the subsequent health monitoring efforts.

Federal data from the World Trade Center Health Program shows that more than 9,400 individuals have died from illnesses linked to exposure to dust and fumes generated by the collapse of the Twin Towers. The newly released records are expected to shed light on the extent of the city’s awareness of air toxicity at the time and may inform ongoing legal and medical inquiries as the nation commemorates the quarter‑century mark of the tragedy.
author: France 24

title: Macron convenes European space summit with low turnout
content:
France is moving forward with a space summit that has drawn little interest from major U.S. technology firms and a weaker than anticipated presence of European heads of state, as President Emmanuel Macron pushes for a more assertive European role in the increasingly competitive domain of space exploration and industry. The summit, scheduled to take place in Paris, is intended to showcase Europe’s capabilities and to foster cooperation among national space agencies, private enterprises, and research institutions.

Organizers report that several leading American companies, including those that dominate satellite communications and launch services, have declined invitations, citing scheduling conflicts and strategic priorities elsewhere. Meanwhile, a number of European leaders have either sent lower‑level delegations or opted not to attend, prompting concerns about the summit’s ability to generate the political momentum Macron envisions. The French government hopes the event will still serve as a platform to discuss regulatory harmonisation, joint investment in launch infrastructure, and the development of a European satellite navigation system that can compete with U.S. and Chinese offerings.

Despite the limited participation, French officials remain confident that the gathering will reinforce Europe’s strategic autonomy in space and lay groundwork for future collaborations. International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley of FRANCE 24 noted that the summit reflects Macron’s broader ambition to position Europe as a key player in the global space race, even as the continent grapples with divergent national interests and external market pressures. The outcomes of the summit are expected to shape policy discussions within the European Union over the coming months.
author: France 24

title: Céline Dion to begin 16‑concert Paris run in September
content:
Céline Dion is set to resume live performances this Saturday in Paris, launching a series of more than 16 concerts scheduled across September and October. The shows represent the singer’s first full‑scale tour dates since stepping back from the road in 2022 after being diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder that limited her ability to perform. At 58, Dion will take the stage in the French capital as part of a highly promoted comeback that has drawn significant attention from fans and media alike.  

The Paris engagements mark a pivotal moment in Dion’s career, signaling her return to a demanding touring schedule after a multi‑year hiatus. Organizers have confirmed that the concerts will be held at the city's major venue, with tickets selling rapidly in advance of the opening night. Industry observers note that the series could set the tone for additional performances in Europe later this year, underscoring Dion’s intent to re‑establish her presence on the international stage despite her health challenges.
author: France 24

title: Kenyan president's remarks cause fear among Burundian refugees
content:
Around 16,000 Burundian refugees and asylum‑seekers are currently residing in Kenya, many of whom sustain themselves through informal occupations such as carpentry, motorcycle‑taxi driving and clothing vending. Since Monday, a significant portion of this community has reported reluctance to attend work and is contemplating departure from the country after remarks made by Kenya’s president triggered widespread apprehension among Burundians. The statements, which have been described by local leaders as hostile, have intensified fears of discrimination and possible legal repercussions for the refugees, prompting humanitarian groups to monitor the situation closely.

Correspondent Bastien Renouil notes that the heightened anxiety has led to a noticeable decline in the presence of Burundian workers in informal markets and transport hubs, with several individuals seeking assistance to relocate either within Kenya or to neighboring states. Authorities have not yet issued an official response to the concerns raised by the refugee community, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees has called for clarification to ensure the safety and livelihoods of the displaced population remain protected.
author: France 24

title: French Legion soldier escapes Colombian guerrilla captivity after month‑long kidnapping
content:
A French Foreign Legion soldier who had been held captive by Colombian guerrillas for almost a month managed to escape, Colombian military officials said. The soldier was taken during an incident earlier this month and remained in the hands of the guerrilla group until he overpowered a guard and fled.

According to a Colombian military source, the soldier subdued his captor, leapt into a river while his hands were still bound, and then navigated the waterway before beginning a four‑day trek across the Andes. He survived the arduous journey through rugged terrain and reached a location where he could be rescued, ending his ordeal.

The military confirmed the soldier’s safe return and indicated that operations to locate and apprehend the guerrilla members involved are ongoing. No further details about the kidnapping or the identity of the guerrilla group were released.
author: France 24

title: Rising Fuel Costs Hit Cambodia's Floating Schools
content:
Fuel prices in Cambodia have risen sharply after the conflict in Iran disrupted global oil supplies, prompting a surge in the cost of diesel and gasoline that many Cambodians depend on for daily activities. The increase has hit families in the country’s fishing communities hardest, as boats and motorized equipment essential for catching fish and transporting goods now require significantly more expenditure. Market analysts attribute the price hike to both the reduced availability of refined petroleum products and the depreciation of the Cambodian riel against the U.S. dollar, which together have driven up import costs for fuel distributors.

The higher fuel costs are also affecting children living around Tonle Sap, the nation’s largest freshwater lake, where many families rely on boat transport to reach schools and markets. With transportation expenses climbing, parents are forced to allocate a larger share of their limited income to fuel, reducing the resources available for school fees, uniforms and supplies. As a result, attendance rates among school‑age children in the lake’s peripheral villages have begun to slip, adding another obstacle to educational attainment in an area already challenged by seasonal flooding and limited infrastructure.
author: DW World

title: 14 Dead in Explosion at Syrian Weapons Depot
content:
An explosion occurred near the Syrian city of Sarmada in Idlib province, located in the country's northwest, according to local authorities. The blast was reported to have struck a site that had been used for the temporary storage of military equipment and war remnants.

The Syrian Defense Ministry confirmed that the location housed weapons and other war material awaiting relocation to a permanent facility. Officials indicated that the stored items were being held temporarily as part of an ongoing effort to consolidate and secure armaments, and they are now planning to move the stockpile to a designated site. No immediate casualties were reported, and security forces have begun an investigation into the cause of the explosion.
author: DW World

title: Ethiopia to adopt presidential system, strengthening Abiy Ahmed's authority
content:
Addis Ababa – Ethiopia’s ruling coalition has announced plans to amend the nation’s constitution to replace its parliamentary framework with a presidential system, a shift that would concentrate executive authority in the office of the prime minister. The proposal, which must pass both houses of parliament and be ratified by a national referendum, outlines a new structure in which the president, elected directly by voters, would serve as both head of state and government, consolidating powers currently divided between the prime minister and the legislature.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who has pursued extensive political and economic reforms since taking office in 2018, stands to gain a stronger mandate under the revised system, according to analysts familiar with the draft. Supporters argue the change could streamline decision‑making and enhance stability, while opposition parties warn it may undermine checks and balances and entrench incumbent power. The government has scheduled public consultations in the coming weeks, with the final amendment expected to be put to a referendum before the end of the year.
author: DW World

title: UN General Assembly opens 81st session, pledges to restore public trust
content:
The United Nations General Assembly opened its 81st session on Tuesday at the UN headquarters in New York, marking the start of a year‑long agenda that confronts a series of global challenges. In his opening remarks, the incoming president of the General Assembly pledged to restore public confidence in the institution, emphasizing the need for transparent and effective action amid ongoing wars, widespread humanitarian emergencies and the accelerating impacts of climate change.  

The president’s commitment comes as member states prepare to debate and adopt resolutions on conflict resolution, aid delivery, and climate mitigation, topics that have dominated recent international discourse. By foregrounding trust‑building measures and coordinated responses, the Assembly aims to reinforce the UN’s role as a central forum for collective problem‑solving throughout the coming year.
author: UN News

title: WFP calls for food assistance in eastern DRC Ebola response
content:
Ebola cases have risen sharply in the eastern provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, prompting health authorities and humanitarian agencies to intensify efforts to meet the basic food needs of affected households. The World Health Organization, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, and several non‑governmental organizations have coordinated the distribution of emergency rations to families in the most impacted health zones, aiming to reduce malnutrition that can exacerbate the virus’s transmission and severity. Food assistance is being delivered alongside vaccination campaigns, contact‑tracing teams, and community education programs to ensure that residents can comply with isolation and treatment protocols without facing immediate hunger.

Officials say that securing reliable nutrition supplies is a critical component of the broader outbreak response, as food insecurity can drive movement of people and undermine public‑health measures. Logistics teams are navigating insecure road networks and occasional armed conflict to reach remote villages, while monitoring mechanisms track the adequacy of food parcels and identify gaps in coverage. The integrated approach seeks to stabilize vulnerable populations, limit further spread of Ebola, and lay the groundwork for a coordinated recovery once the outbreak is contained.
author: UN News

title: AI data centres strain global electricity systems
content:
The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) has issued a warning that the rapid expansion of data‑intensive technologies, especially artificial‑intelligence (AI) data centres, is outpacing the capacity of existing electricity infrastructure. In a recent assessment, the commission highlighted that the surge in power demand from AI‑driven computing facilities is creating a mismatch with the pace of upgrades to generation, transmission and distribution networks, raising questions about the future reliability and resilience of global energy systems.

UNECE officials noted that the imbalance could lead to heightened stress on power grids, increased risk of outages, and the need for substantial investment in renewable generation and grid modernization to accommodate the growing load. The commission called for coordinated policy measures, accelerated development of sustainable energy sources, and strategic planning to ensure that electricity supply can keep pace with the expanding digital economy, thereby safeguarding energy security worldwide.
author: UN News

title: UN chief urges Israel to withdraw from Lebanon as fighting intensifies in Nabatieh
content:
The United Nations Secretary‑General has condemned the rising number of civilian casualties in southern Lebanon and urged Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanese territory as hostilities intensify around the city of Nabatieh. In a statement issued today, he highlighted the humanitarian impact of the fighting and called for immediate steps to protect civilians in accordance with international humanitarian law.

The Secretary‑General’s appeal follows a recent surge in cross‑border exchanges between Israeli and Lebanese armed groups, which has led to heightened military activity in the Nabatieh region and surrounding villages. He reiterated the UN’s longstanding position that any use of force must be proportionate and directed solely at combatants, and urged both parties to pursue de‑escalation measures to prevent further loss of life. The call for withdrawal and restraint comes amid growing international concern over the conflict’s spill‑over effects and the need for a durable cease‑fire.
author: UN News

title: Global shipping faces rising risks as vessels and crews become leverage in unrelated conflicts
content:
The global shipping sector is confronting what industry analysts describe as a “genuinely unprecedented” convergence of maritime crises. Recent weeks have seen a sharp rise in incidents where commercial vessels and their crews are being employed as strategic leverage in geopolitical disputes unrelated to maritime trade, intensifying risks across major shipping lanes.

Incidents ranging from the targeting of container ships in the Red Sea to the seizure of vessels near the Black Sea illustrate the expanding scope of the threat. Nations and non‑state actors have increasingly used the disruption of cargo flows to exert political pressure, prompting insurers to raise premiums and operators to adopt longer, costlier routes. The resulting operational strain is affecting global supply chains, with delays reported in the delivery of essential commodities and heightened concerns for the safety and welfare of seafarers who now face heightened exposure to conflict‑related hazards.

Industry bodies and governments are responding with coordinated security advisories, expanded naval escorts, and calls for diplomatic resolutions to de‑escalate the use of shipping as a bargaining chip. Continued escalation could further destabilize international trade, underscoring the need for swift multilateral action to safeguard maritime commerce and protect the personnel who navigate it.
author: UN News

title: Record attacks on schools leave 93 million children out of class, UN warns
content:
September usually heralds the beginning of the school year for millions of students in the northern hemisphere, yet education experts warned on Wednesday that an estimated 93 million children remain out of the classroom. The figure reflects a surge in attacks on learning environments, including bombings, raids, and other forms of violence that have disrupted schooling across conflict‑affected regions. Data compiled by international monitoring bodies show that the number of children denied access to education has risen sharply in recent months, surpassing previous records for school‑related attacks.

The unprecedented scale of the crisis has prompted calls from governments, NGOs, and intergovernmental agencies for stronger protective measures and rapid restoration of educational services. Stakeholders emphasize that safeguarding schools and ensuring continuity of learning are essential to prevent long‑term socioeconomic repercussions for the affected youth. The situation underscores the urgent need for coordinated international action to secure safe learning spaces for all children.
author: UN News

title: UN Secretary-General calls on leaders to invest in peace amid rising conflicts
content:
The United Nations Secretary‑General issued an appeal on Wednesday urging governments and other decision‑makers to increase investment in peacebuilding as escalating violence, societal division and armed conflict intensify human suffering across the globe. Speaking at a high‑level gathering in New York, he highlighted that the cumulative impact of wars in Ukraine, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the turmoil in Sudan and other flashpoints is eroding development gains and deepening poverty, displacement and loss of life.

In his remarks, the Secretary‑General called for a coordinated approach that channels greater resources into preventive diplomacy, mediation, and the strengthening of UN peacekeeping and peace‑building operations. He emphasized that sustained financial support and political commitment are essential to address the root causes of conflict and to integrate peace objectives into broader development and climate agendas. The appeal concluded with a request that world leaders prioritize peace as a strategic investment to mitigate further hardship and promote long‑term stability.
author: UN News

title: Hurricane Lowell leaves 30,000 without power as Kauai faces flooding
content:
Kauai is contending with extensive flooding and hazardous debris after Hurricane Lowell struck the western coast of Hawaii overnight. The storm, which intensified to a Category 2 hurricane as it approached the islands, brought sustained winds of up to 110 mph and torrential rain that overwhelmed low‑lying areas and riverbanks across the island’s northern and western districts.

State and local emergency officials have deployed rescue teams, sandbags, and road‑clearing equipment to address the damage, while urging residents to avoid travel on affected routes and to stay clear of downed power lines and floating debris. Power outages have been reported in several communities, and shelters have been opened for displaced families. Authorities continue to monitor water levels and forecast further rain, emphasizing that recovery efforts will persist throughout the coming days as the island works to restore infrastructure and ensure public safety.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza students with foreign university offers blocked by immigration rules
content:
As the new academic term begins, thousands of students who have secured places at overseas institutions are confronting immigration requirements that many describe as “impossible” to meet. Recent changes to visa policy – including a higher points threshold, tighter English‑language criteria and a reduction in the number of student visas allocated for certain countries – have taken effect just weeks before the start of courses. The timing leaves little room for applicants to gather the additional documentation or meet the accelerated deadlines, prompting several university admissions offices to report a surge in deferments and withdrawals.

Education bodies and student unions have warned that the new rules could jeopardise the enrolment of an entire cohort, undermining both individual academic plans and the financial commitments of partner institutions abroad. Officials from the Department for Education acknowledged the challenges and indicated that a review of the implementation schedule is under consideration, while universities are urging authorities to provide a clear pathway for affected students. The situation remains fluid, and stakeholders are awaiting further guidance on whether the immigration framework will be adjusted before the semester progresses.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bangladesh measles outbreak kills over 1,000 children, infects nearly 190,000
content:
Dhaka – Bangladesh is confronting its most severe measles outbreak on record, with the health ministry reporting 1,002 child fatalities and close to 190,000 confirmed cases since the start of March. The surge, which the ministry describes as the worst in the country’s recent history, has prompted the government to declare a public health emergency and to mobilize emergency vaccination drives in the most affected districts, including Dhaka, Chittagong and Sylhet.

Health officials attribute the rapid spread to gaps in routine immunisation coverage, exacerbated by disruptions to health services during the COVID‑19 pandemic. The World Health Organization has dispatched technical teams to assist with surveillance, case management and the procurement of measles‑containing vaccines, while the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has urged parents to ensure children receive the recommended two‑dose schedule. Ongoing efforts aim to curb transmission and prevent further loss of life as the outbreak continues to unfold.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel responds to UK trade ban on illegal settlements
content:
London has announced a new trade restriction that bars the import of goods produced in Israeli settlements deemed illegal under international law, a move spearheaded by the United Kingdom and supported by several European partners. The policy, which took effect this week, targets products originating from West Bank areas that the United Nations and most of the international community consider occupied territory, and it aligns the UK with the European Union’s broader strategy to curb economic activity that may legitimize settlement expansion.

Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the decision, describing it as “unfair and politically motivated,” and warned that it could strain bilateral relations that have traditionally been close. Israeli officials have indicated that reciprocal measures may be considered, while the UK government has defended the ban as consistent with its commitment to uphold international law and human‑rights standards. Analysts note that the development adds pressure to an already delicate diplomatic landscape, and both sides are expected to engage in further talks to manage the fallout and assess the impact on trade and cooperation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK sanctions Israeli settlements but analysts say measures are insufficient for Palestinian statehood
content:
London – The United Kingdom’s recent diplomatic initiative aimed at advancing Palestinian statehood has been judged by experts as insufficient to generate substantial momentum for the cause. In a statement delivered at the United Nations General Assembly, the British Foreign Secretary affirmed support for a two‑state solution and pledged to explore the possibility of formally recognising a Palestinian state, while also calling for renewed negotiations between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.

Analysts highlighted that the UK’s approach, which stops short of an outright recognition and lacks accompanying measures such as increased humanitarian aid, settlement activity restrictions, or a clear roadmap for negotiations, falls short of the decisive action needed to shift the stalled peace process. They noted that symbolic endorsements without concrete policy steps are unlikely to alter the dynamics on the ground or persuade other key actors, such as the United States and the European Union, to adopt a more proactive stance.

The assessment suggests that, unless the United Kingdom couples its verbal support with substantive policy initiatives, the prospect of accelerating Palestinian statehood remains limited. Observers will be watching for any further developments from London that could translate diplomatic rhetoric into actionable progress in the broader Middle‑East peace effort.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid Champions League live updates
content:
The league phase clash between Manchester United and Liverpool at Old Trafford on Saturday marked the 12th round of the Premier League season, drawing significant attention after both clubs secured points in their previous fixtures. Manchester United entered the match on a three‑point streak, bolstered by the return of midfielder Paul Pogba from injury, while Liverpool sought to rebound from a 1‑0 defeat to Chelsea, relying on the form of forward Mohamed Salah, who had netted four goals in the last two games. Pre‑match expectations highlighted United’s 4‑3‑3 formation aimed at exploiting the flanks, contrasted with Liverpool’s 4‑2‑3‑1 setup designed to press high and dominate possession.

The first half unfolded with United pressing aggressively, creating early chances through wing‑back Luke Shaw’s crosses, but Liverpool’s defense held firm, with goalkeeper Alisson making a crucial save in the 22nd minute. At the 37th minute, a quick transition saw Salah receive a through ball from Jordan Henderson and slot the ball past David de Gea, giving Liverpool a 1‑0 lead. The second half saw United increase tempo, and a corner in the 58th minute was headed in by Harry Maguire, equalising the score. Momentum shifted again in the 74th minute when Liverpool’s midfielder Fabinho intercepted a pass and delivered a low drive to Diogo Jota, who finished to restore the lead. The match concluded with Liverpool holding a 2‑1 advantage, securing three points and moving to 28 points in the table, while United remained on 24 points, trailing by two positions.

The result leaves Liverpool in contention for a top‑four finish, with their next fixture against Aston Villa offering an opportunity to extend their winning run. Manchester United will look to regroup ahead of their upcoming clash with Tottenham Hotspur, aiming to recover lost ground in the league standings. Both clubs are expected to assess tactical adjustments and squad rotations as the season progresses toward its decisive stages.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Armed group attacks teacher training centre in Wum, kills police officer and kidnaps teachers
content:
An armed group launched an assault on a teacher‑training centre in the town of Wum, the capital of Cameroon’s Northwest Region, the regional governor said. The attack, which occurred early on Wednesday, targeted the facility that provides professional development for educators serving the Anglophone community.

The governor, who did not identify the perpetrators, confirmed that security forces have been deployed to the site and are conducting investigations. He urged residents to remain calm and cooperate with authorities as they work to secure the area and assess any injuries or damage. The incident adds to a series of violent episodes in the region, which has experienced heightened tension between government forces and separatist factions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arsenal vs Napoli Champions League live match updates
content:
Arsenal have kicked off their UEFA Champions League campaign, opening the group stage against Bayer Leverkusen at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday. The English side, entering the competition as one of the tournament’s favourites, will look to build on their domestic form after securing a top‑four finish in the Premier League last season. The match, scheduled for a 20:00 GMT kickoff, marks the first of six group fixtures for Arsenal, who were drawn in Group C alongside Bayer Leverkusen, Napoli and Red Bull Salzburg.

Live text commentary of the encounter will be provided throughout the game, offering minute‑by‑minute updates for fans following the action online. The coverage will highlight key moments such as goals, substitutions, tactical changes and disciplinary incidents, allowing supporters to stay informed in real time. Arsenal’s performance in this opening fixture will set the tone for their pursuit of a deep run in Europe, with the club aiming to progress to the knockout stages and ultimately contend for the title.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella ends ten-year firearm permit suspension
content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the termination of a ten‑year suspension on permits to carry legal firearms, restoring the ability of qualified citizens to obtain and renew such authorizations. The decision was disclosed during a press briefing held at the presidential palace, where officials indicated that the policy shift aligns with recent revisions to the nation’s firearms regulations.

The suspension, originally imposed in 2014, had halted the issuance of new permits and the renewal of existing ones, affecting private security operators, sport shooters, and individuals meeting statutory criteria. Under the new directive, the Ministry of the Interior will reopen the application process, requiring standard background checks, mandatory safety training, and compliance with updated storage guidelines. Authorities have indicated that the reinstatement will be carried out in phases to ensure administrative capacity and public safety oversight.

The reversal is expected to re‑enable lawful firearm ownership while subjecting applicants to the revised regulatory framework. Government representatives affirmed that monitoring mechanisms will be strengthened to track compliance and address any emerging concerns.
author: BBC World

title: Uganda withdraws from Invictus Games, defence chief announces
content:
The chief of defence announced today that a final decision has been made regarding Uganda’s involvement in the upcoming regional joint military exercise, a move that follows Uganda’s statement two months earlier that it intended to take part. The announcement was delivered at a press briefing in the capital, where the defence chief confirmed that the participating forces will be finalized within the next fortnight.

The decision comes as the exercise, slated to begin in early December, aims to enhance interoperability among East African Community militaries and to address shared security challenges such as cross‑border insurgency and illicit trafficking. Ugandan officials had previously indicated a willingness to contribute a mechanised battalion and logistical support, and the latest ruling clarifies the scale and timing of that contribution. Regional partners welcomed the clarification, noting that a definitive roster will allow for detailed planning of joint operations and training modules.

In concluding remarks, the chief of defence emphasized that the finalized arrangement reflects a coordinated approach to regional defense readiness and will be communicated to all member states ahead of the exercise’s launch. Further updates are expected as the participating nations confirm their troop deployments and logistical arrangements.
author: BBC World

title: China to launch Mars sample-return mission in 2028
content:
China’s space agency has reported significant progress on the Tianwen‑3 Mars sample‑return mission, which is slated for launch in 2028. The project will send a lander and rover to the Red Planet, collect soil and rock samples, and return them to Earth in 2031. Engineers have confirmed that the spacecraft’s return vehicle is now capable of re‑entering Earth’s atmosphere and safely delivering the samples to a designated recovery site.

The mission follows the successful Tianwen‑1 orbiter and rover, marking China’s third major Mars endeavor. By targeting a 2031 return, Tianwen‑3 will join a growing international effort to bring extraterrestrial material back to Earth, enabling detailed laboratory analysis of Martian geology and potential biosignatures. The completion of key subsystem tests brings the program closer to its launch window, underscoring China’s expanding capabilities in deep‑space exploration.
author: Space.com

title: Shane Richie Pleads Not Guilty to Drink-Driving Charge
content:
A 62‑year‑old actor was taken into custody by police on the forecourt of a petrol station in July 2026.  The arrest occurred during a routine stop at the service station, and the actor’s identity has not yet been released to the public.  Police said the detention was part of an ongoing investigation into alleged misconduct, though no specific charges have been announced.

According to the Metropolitan Police, the actor was detained following a review of evidence that prompted a formal inquiry.  He was transported to the nearest police station where he was processed and placed under arrest.  The actor is expected to appear before a magistrate in the coming weeks, and the Crown Prosecution Service will decide whether to bring formal charges.

The investigation is continuing, and authorities have stated that further information will be released as the case progresses.  The public is advised to await official statements before drawing conclusions.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Sinkhole Opens in Nicolas Cage’s Malibu Home After Heavy Rain
content:
A 30‑foot crater suddenly opened outside an actor’s Malibu residence after a bout of heavy rain in Southern California. The unexpected sinkhole appeared on the property’s driveway, creating a deep, circular depression that startled neighbors and prompted an immediate response from local emergency services.

City officials and geologists are investigating the cause, noting that the area has experienced significant rainfall in recent days, which can trigger rapid underground water movement and weaken soil structure. The Malibu Police Department has secured the site and issued a warning for residents to avoid the crater while experts assess the stability of the surrounding ground. No injuries have been reported, and the actor’s home remains occupied.

The investigation is ongoing, with state and local agencies coordinating to determine whether additional sinkholes or subsidence risks exist in the vicinity. Residents are advised to monitor updates from the Malibu Police Department and to follow any temporary safety orders issued by the county.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: NFL 2026: Teams That Could Challenge the Rams
content:
The NFL’s 2026 season opens on Wednesday night, and the league’s writers are already weighing in on the most anticipated storylines. Among the topics highlighted are the battle for the league’s most valuable player, the top rookies to watch, and the potential disasters that could unfold as teams adjust to a new season of high‑stakes matchups. The focus, however, remains on the evolving role of the quarterback, particularly the shift back toward more snaps taken directly under center.

For years the NFL has become a “shotgun” league, with quarterbacks taking the majority of their snaps three to seven yards behind the center. Recent data from the 2025 season, however, shows a marked uptick in efficiency when quarterbacks snap the ball directly under center. Players such as Matthew Stafford, Caleb Williams, and Sam Darnold led the charge, posting higher completion percentages and lower interception rates on those plays. Coaches who have begun to emphasize this approach are seeing measurable gains, and the trend is expected to spread as other teams look to replicate the success.

As the season gets underway, analysts will watch to see whether the increased use of center snaps translates into sustained success for the teams that adopt it. While the shotgun remains the dominant offensive philosophy, the evidence from 2025 suggests that a balanced approach—blending shotgun and under‑center plays—could become a new standard in quarterback deployment. The outcome of this strategic shift will likely influence both individual player performances and overall team competitiveness as the season progresses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: County Championship Day Two: Leicestershire v Somerset and Nottinghamshire v Hampshire
content:
The County Championship title race is picking up steam as Sussex host Surrey at Hove, a match that has drawn attention from all corners of the competition. With the standings tightening, every game is now a potential turning point for the teams vying for the top spot.

Sussex won the toss and elected to bat first, a decision that appears aimed at avoiding the threat of Surrey’s Indian left‑arm spinner Mahipal Lomror, who is slated to bowl early. The Sussex openers struggled, losing wickets quickly and finding themselves 16‑0 at the crease. Meanwhile, Ben Aitchison of Surrey has been a consistent performer for the season, and his presence at the crease has been a focal point for the opposition. Kent’s recent victory over Crawley, where they secured a 22‑2 win, has added another layer of intrigue to the title chase, as teams look to build momentum.

The early collapse for Sussex could have implications for their campaign, but the match remains in the balance. Both sides will be looking to capitalize on any advantage as the championship progresses, with the next fixtures set to test the resilience of the title contenders.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Trump Leverages Sports to Shape Public Narrative
content:
President Donald Trump has recently shifted his public focus toward sports, with a particular emphasis on golf. This pivot aligns with a broader pattern of narrowing interests that includes high‑profile projects in Washington, D.C., and a preference for conflicts that he believes can be resolved swiftly. The emphasis on golf has become a recurring theme in his public appearances and media engagements.

In the same vein, author Leander Schaerlaeckens has released *The Long Game: U. S. Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four‑Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts*. The book chronicles the evolution of the U.S. men’s national soccer team over forty years, offering analysis of its challenges and successes. Schaerlaeckens, a faculty member at Marist University, provides a scholarly perspective on the sport’s development and its cultural impact in the United States.

The convergence of political messaging and sports coverage continues to shape public discourse. While Trump’s use of golf as a platform underscores his personal brand, the publication of Schaerlaeckens’ book contributes to the broader narrative of American sports history, illustrating how athletic endeavors remain a significant lens through which national identity and ambition are examined.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Extend Borthwick Contract Until 2028 Six Nations
content:
The Rugby Football Union (RFU) has taken steps to secure stability for England’s campaign ahead of next year’s Rugby World Cup.
